newsitem.title: IRAN: Iran says no Iraqi word on holy shrines visits.
newsitem.headline: Iran says no Iraqi word on holy shrines visits.

text.p: Iraq has not officially informed Iran of its decision to allow visits by Iranians to Iraq's Shi'ite Moslem shrines, suspended since the start of the 1980-88 war, an Iranian official was quoted on Tuesday as saying.

"We have not been informed officially and therefore we cannot take a specific stance. We are waiting for the Iraqi officials to communicate the matter to us," Iran's Foreign Ministry spokesman Mahmoud Mohammadi said.
His comments were carried by the English-langauge Iran News.
Baghdad Radio on Monday said Iraqi President Saddam Hussein had decided to allow the visits to resume from September 4.

Shi'ites, who form the overwhelming majority of Iran's 60 million population, regard the shrines in Karbala and Najaf in southern Iraq as second only to Islam's holiest sites in Mecca and Medina in Saudi Arabia.

Iranian visits to the shrines were halted at the start of the war in which nearly one million people from Iran and Iraq died. September 4 is the date Iraq says the war started in 1980. Iran says it began on September 22.
Iraq said the decision was taken despite problems still troubling Iraq's relations with Iran.
Saddam has urged Iran's new president, Mohammad Khatami, to free Iraqi prisoners of war and return to Iraq aircraft sent to Iran to escape bombings during the 1991 Gulf War over Kuwait.
He said Iraq had freed all 39,000 Iranian POWs except for one pilot whose plane was shot down over Iraqi territory on September 18, 1980.
Khatami had urged Iraq to free Iranian prisoners of war.
Iraq says more than 20,000 Iraqis are still held in Iran. Tehran denies this and says Baghdad is still holding 5,000 to 10,000 Iranian prisoners.
